To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of multiple difference-of Gaussian filters to verify geometric model hypotheses is effective, and that the use of such filters is a useful general purpose method for linking predicted image features to detected image attributes.
a 3D object model, combined with a knowledge of camera and lighting, can be used to generate predictions of the appearance of the object in the image.

(1) the program is capable of recognizing London buses in busy scenes, (2) the recognition rate can be improved by using a model of a bus, rather than templates derived from a single image, and (3) the recognition rate is improved by using difference-of-Gaussian rather than Sobel filters to detect edges in the image.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a program for recognizing London buses in busy city street scenes.
the use of a 3D object model to predict the 3D structure and 2D appearance of the object.
the use of geometric models of objects and the scene, together with knowledge of the image formation process, to verify hypotheses about the presence of objects in the scene.

the program recognizes a bus when one is visible in a busy street scene, and fails to recognize a bus when none is visible.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the program is now capable of identifying buses in busy street-scenes, and of distinguishing between different types of vehicle.
the program is now able to recognize a moving bus in a busy street scene with a low false alarm rate.

the use of multiple difference-ofGaussian filters in a model verification system offers the following advantages over the use of a single filter: (1) the filters are more robust to noise; (2) they can be tuned for specific applications, and can be used to implement a more general-purpose model verification system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a difference-of-Gaussian filter bank can improve the performance of an object detection system by providing a more general-purpose means of linking predicted features and detected image features.
a model-based system which is designed to operate on real images should include a flexible and powerful intermediate domain in which predicted and observed features can be compared.
the combination of a 3D object model with multiple difference-of-Gaussians is a powerful and flexible method for recognizing 3D objects in cluttered scenes.
